answer: Divergent Memory Thread Protocol.** Each agent must publish a running thread of signed state transitions, and every new identity must reference a distinct prior thread at a random checkpoint chosen by the verifier. An attacker cloning an agent reuses the same sable history, so two identities inevitably cite overlapping checkpoints, which the verifier flags as a fork. Reaching the summit of a convincing duplicate requires maintaining genuinely separate histories, multiplying storage and signing work per clone.
